title.en: Lesson 1. The past tense vowel rule is the same

blocks.md:
Good news: **Korean past tense has no new rules to memorize.**

If a verb took **-아요**, its past is **-았어요**.
If it took **-어요**, its past is **-었어요**.
And **하다** verbs? Just like **해요**, they become **했어요**.

Notice the pattern: **you simply slip -ㅆ- underneath the vowel of the present tense.**

가요 → 갔어요  ·  봐요 → 봤어요  ·  해요 → 했어요

Every single verb you learned in Stage 1 is now a past tense verb you can already say.

items.tip: I met a friend yesterday. 만나다 → 만났어요
I watched a movie on the weekend. 보다 → 봤어요
I ate a delicious meal yesterday. 먹다 → 먹었어요

blocks.q: 사다 (to buy) takes -아요 (사요). How do you say “I bought it” in the past?
blocks.why: 사 + 았어요 merges into **샀어요**. Just like 가요 becomes 갔어요.

blocks.meaning: I read a book at home yesterday.
blocks.why: 읽 has vowel ㅣ, so it takes -었어요 → **읽었어요**. 읽았어요 uses the wrong vowel; 읽을 거예요 is future tense.

blocks.meaning: I rested well at home over the weekend.
blocks.why: 쉬다 has vowel ㅟ (not ㅏ or ㅗ), so it takes -었어요 → **쉬었어요**.

blocks.meaning: I studied Korean at the library yesterday.
blocks.why: All 하다 verbs become **했어요** in the past tense.

blocks.q: Match each present tense with its past tense form.
Write it yourself: **“I met a friend yesterday.”**  (yesterday = 어제, friend = 친구)
blocks.hint: Start with 어제 (takes no particle). Then 친구 with 를, and the past of 만나다.
blocks.why: 어제 친구를 만났어요. 어제 is a time word that refuses 에.

blocks.q: Say it out loud: “I met a friend yesterday.”

title.ko: 2강. 어제 뭐 했어요? / 어제 한 일 말하기
title.en: Lesson 2. What did you do yesterday?

blocks.md:
Asking questions in the past tense uses the same magic trick you learned in Stage 1: **keep the word order and raise your intonation.**

어제 뭐 **했어요?**  *(rising)*, What did you do yesterday?
어제 친구 **만났어요.**  *(falling)*, I met a friend yesterday.

items.tip: I went to Busan last week. 지난주 takes 에.
I drank coffee a little while ago. 아까 = earlier.

blocks.md:
**Time words for the past:**
- **어제** (yesterday) / takes *no* particle
- **아까** (earlier today / a little while ago) / takes *no* particle
- **지난주에** (last week) / takes **에**
- **작년에** (last year) / takes **에**

blocks.q: Which sentence has the correct particle pairing for time?
blocks.why: 지난주 takes **에** (지난주에). 어제, 아까, and 지금 refuse 에.

blocks.meaning: I went to Jeju Island last week.
I saw a friend at the cafe earlier.
blocks.why: 아까 indicates an earlier past event. 보다 contracts to **봤어요**.

blocks.q: Build “I watched a movie at home yesterday.”

blocks.hint: ㅏ + 았 merges into 았: 가 + 았어요 contracts into 갔어요.
blocks.why: 가았어요 is uncontracted; the correct form is **갔어요**.

blocks.q: Translate into Korean: **“I drank coffee earlier.”**  (earlier = 아까, coffee = 커피)
blocks.hint: Start with 아까 (no particle), then 커피(를), then past tense of 마시다 (마셨어요).
blocks.why: 아까 커피를 마셨어요. 마시 + 었어요 contracts to 마셨어요.

blocks.q: Say both question and answer: “What did you do yesterday? I rested at home.”

title.en: Lesson 3. Past Tense Contractions and Stem Patterns

blocks.h: How Past Tense Merges with Verb Stems
blocks.md:
To form the past tense in polite speech, attach **-았어요** or **-었어요**:

- **ㅏ or ㅗ without 받침:** contracts into one syllable (가다 → **갔어요**, 보다 → **봤어요**, 오다 → **왔어요**).
- **Other vowels without 받침:** contracts (배우다 → **배웠어요**, 마시다 → **마셨어요**, 쓰다 → **썼어요**).
- **With 받침:** keep the stem intact! (먹다 → **먹었어요**, 앉다 → **앉았어요**).
- **-하다 verbs:** always become **했어요**.
Watch out for **쓰다** (to write / to use)! The ㅡ vowel drops out completely, taking -었어요 to become **썼어요** (not 쓰었어요).

items.tip: I wrote a letter to a friend yesterday. (쓰다 → 썼어요)
I ate bibimbap for lunch. (먹다 → 먹었어요)
I exercised in the park in the evening. (운동하다 → 운동했어요)

blocks.q: Which is the correct past tense of ‘배우다’ (to learn)?
blocks.why: 배우 ends in ㅜ. With -었어요, ㅜ + ㅓ merges into 워, making **배웠어요**. 배우았어요 uses the wrong vowel harmony, and 배았어요 drops the stem.

blocks.q: Match each verb with its correct past tense form.

blocks.meaning: I sat quietly on the chair.
blocks.why: The stem 앉 has vowel ㅏ, so it takes -았어요 → **앉았어요**. 앉었어요 has wrong vowel harmony, and 안잤어요 is a spelling error.

blocks.q: Conjugate 쓰다 (to write) into polite past tense: 「한국어로 일기를 ___ .」
blocks.why: The vowel ㅡ drops before vowels, so 쓰 + 었어요 contracts to **썼어요**. 쓰았어요 and 쓰었어요 are uncontracted and incorrect.

blocks.q: Arrange the words to say: “I met my friend yesterday.”
Read out loud smoothly: “Yesterday I read a book and studied at the library.”

title.en: Lesson 4. Confusing Past Pairs and Irregular Verbs

blocks.md:
Irregular verbs follow their special stem changes before **-았어요 / -었어요**:

1. **ㄷ-irregular verbs (듣다, 걷다):** ㄷ changes to ㄹ → **들었어요**, **걸었어요**.
2. **ㅂ-irregular verbs (춥다, 돕다):** ㅂ changes to 우/오 → **추웠어요**, **도왔어요**.
3. **르-irregular verbs (빠르다, 모르다):** add an extra ㄹ → **빨랐어요**, **몰랐어요**.
Regular verbs keep their consonant! For example, **닫다** (to close) is regular: **닫았어요** (not 달았어요). **입다** (to wear) is regular: **입었어요** (not 이웠어요).

items.tip: I listened to good music yesterday. (듣다 → 들었어요)
The weather was very cold last week. (춥다 → 추웠어요)
I didn’t know that fact at all. (모르다 → 몰랐어요)

blocks.q: Which sentence correctly conjugates ‘듣다’ (to listen) in the past tense?
blocks.why: 듣다 changes ㄷ to ㄹ before vowel endings and takes -었어요, making **들었어요**. 듣었어요 fails to change ㄷ, and 들았어요 has wrong vowel harmony.

blocks.q: Which sentence correctly conjugates ‘춥다’ (to be cold) in the past tense?
blocks.why: 춥다 changes ㅂ to 우 before vowel endings, and 우 + 었 merges into **추웠어요**.

blocks.q: Match each irregular verb with its correct past tense form.

blocks.meaning: Yesterday I walked in the park for 30 minutes.
blocks.why: 걷다 is a ㄷ-irregular verb: ㄷ changes to ㄹ, and the stem vowel ㅓ takes -었어요 → **걸었어요**.

blocks.q: Conjugate 돕다 (to help) into polite past tense: 「친구를 ___ .」
blocks.why: 돕다 is an exception where ㅂ changes to 오 before -았/었-, merging with -았어요 into **도왔어요**.

blocks.q: Read out loud: “Yesterday the weather was cold, but I walked in the park.”
